title: How Does Your Phone Know It's Your Fingerprint?
sources: Apple Support, 'About Touch ID advanced security technology' (support.apple.com/105095): the sensor uses capacitive touch to take a high-resolution image of small sections of the fingerprint; only a mathematical representation is stored, never images; the data is protected by the Secure Enclave, never stored on Apple servers or backed up to iCloud; when you touch it again it compares against the enrolled data

Kintronics, 'How Fingerprint Readers Work': capacitive sensors measure the variation in capacitance created by the distance of the ridges and valleys from the sensor surface; matching uses key data points (minutiae) from the pattern
NIST / standard biometrics usage: fingerprint minutiae are ridge endings and ridge bifurcations (where a ridge line ends or splits)

Live Science, 'Do identical twins have identical fingerprints?' (2021): identical twins do not have identical fingerprints; prints form between 13 and 19 weeks of fetal development; DNA plays a major role but position in the womb, nutrients and umbilical cord length also affect them

lines.text: How does your phone know it's your finger, and not mine?
lines.caps: HOW DOES YOUR *PHONE | KNOW IT'S *YOUR FINGER | AND NOT *MINE?

lines.text: Well, your fingertip is covered in tiny ridges,
lines.caps: WELL YOUR *FINGERTIP | IS COVERED IN TINY *RIDGES

lines.text: and the sensor under it is a grid of tiny electric pixels.
lines.caps: AND THE *SENSOR | UNDER IT IS A *GRID | OF TINY ELECTRIC *PIXELS

lines.text: Ridges touch the sensor, but valleys leave tiny air gaps,
lines.caps: *RIDGES | TOUCH THE *SENSOR | BUT *VALLEYS | LEAVE TINY AIR *GAPS

lines.text: so each pixel reads a different charge, and that draws your print.
lines.caps: SO EACH *PIXEL | READS A DIFFERENT *CHARGE | AND THAT *DRAWS | YOUR *PRINT

lines.text: But it doesn't keep a photo.
It marks the spots where lines end or split, and saves them as math,
lines.caps: IT MARKS THE *SPOTS | WHERE LINES *END | OR *SPLIT | AND SAVES THEM AS *MATH

lines.text: locked in a secure chip that never leaves your phone.
lines.caps: LOCKED IN A *SECURE CHIP | THAT NEVER *LEAVES | YOUR *PHONE

lines.text: Touch it again, and if the points match, you're in.
lines.caps: TOUCH IT *AGAIN | AND IF THE *POINTS | *MATCH | YOU'RE *IN

lines.text: The twist? Even identical twins have different fingerprints,
because the womb shapes them too, not just your DNA.
lines.caps: BECAUSE THE *WOMB | SHAPES THEM *TOO | NOT JUST YOUR *DNA

lines.text: So your finger is a password nobody else was born with.
lines.caps: SO YOUR *FINGER | IS A *PASSWORD | NOBODY ELSE WAS *BORN WITH
